newsitem.title: USA: Fuisz Technologies sees Q4, 96 yr loss.
newsitem.headline: Fuisz Technologies sees Q4, 96 yr loss.

text.p: Fuisz Technologies said Monday it expects to report a loss for the fourth quarter and the year because McNeil Consumer Products, a Johnson & Johnson division, has decided against using Fuisz technology to develop nutritional supplements.
The stock fell Monday morning from 13-7/8 to trade near 10.
On Monday the company reported a third quarter loss of $0.11 per share, compared to a loss of $0.18 per share in the year-ago quarter.
Fuisz completed its initial public offering in December 1995.
Chief Executive Richard Fuisz said later that Johnson & Johnson's decision has a net effect on the company of $4 million.

Fuisz said his company has signed a letter of intent with another partner for its nutraceuticals, a category of products that include baby formula and vitamins. The new agreement would give Fuisz co-marketing rights, which the option with Johnson & Johnson did not, Fuisz said.
"The company is better off in fact with a new partner, and the net effect on earnings is relatively minor for a company such as us," Fuisz said.
Fuisz said he could not disclose the name of the new co-marketing partner, but would "as soon as we can."
Fuisz Technologies reported revenues of about $5.7 million in fiscal 1995.
